questions.def: When 'neither/nor' connects singular subjects, the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
questions.question: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ happy with the results.

questions.def: The subject of the participle clause must be the same as the main clause.
questions.question: Having finished the exam, ___.

questions.def: 'Despite' does not require 'of'. 'In spite of' does.
questions.question: Despite of the rain, we decided to go for a walk.

questions.def: The past tense of 'lie' (to recline) is 'lay'.
questions.question: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon.

questions.def: Committee acting individually takes plural verb.
questions.question: The committee ___ divided in their opinion on the matter.

questions.def: 'It's high time' is followed by the past simple.
questions.question: It's high time you ___ studying for the exam.

questions.def: 'Affect' is a verb meaning to influence.
questions.question: The new policy will ___ all employees.

questions.def: 'Wish' about the past uses past perfect.
questions.question: I wish I ___ more attention in class.

questions.def: 'Be used to' + gerund means accustomed to.
questions.question: He is used ___ early every morning.

questions.def: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If I ___, I would have helped you.

questions.def: 'Scarcely' requires inversion and is followed by 'when'.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ the house when it started raining.

questions.def: 'Look forward to' is followed by a gerund.
questions.question: She is looking forward ___ you next week.

questions.def: 'Advise' is a verb; 'advice' is a noun.
questions.question: I strongly ___ you to take the course.

questions.def: Double comparatives: 'The more... the more...'
questions.question: The more you study, ___ you will understand.

questions.def: 'Be said to' + infinitive.
questions.question: He is said ___ the best player in the team.

questions.def: Third conditional: would have + past participle 'lost'.
questions.question: If you hadn't been driving so fast, you wouldn't have ___ control.

questions.def: 'Not only' at the beginning requires inversion.
questions.question: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot his book.

questions.def: 'Would rather' for past wishes takes past perfect.
questions.question: I'd rather you ___ me the truth earlier.

questions.def: Verb of perception (heard) + object + bare infinitive/present participle.
questions.question: I ___ him singing in the shower.

questions.def: 'As if/though' introduce a subjunctive mood.
questions.question: He behaves ___ he were the boss.

questions.def: 'Prevent' is followed by 'from' + gerund.
questions.question: They prevented him ___ leaving the country.

questions.def: 'Permitted' is the past participle used as an adjective.
questions.question: Smoking is not ___ in this area.

questions.def: 'Appreciate' is followed by a gerund.
questions.question: I would appreciate ___ from you soon.

questions.def: 'Insist' + 'that' clause uses the subjunctive 'be'.
questions.question: She insisted that he ___ present at the meeting.

questions.def: 'Despite' needs a gerund after it, not an infinitive or past participle.
questions.question: Despite ___ tired, she finished the race.

questions.def: 'Wish' about the past uses past perfect to express regret.
questions.question: I wish I ___ more time to travel last year.

questions.def: Regular verb 'advise' in the past simple is 'advised'.
questions.question: The doctor ___ him to stop smoking.

questions.def: The correct preposition to use with 'good' and a gerund is 'at'.
questions.question: She is good ___ playing the piano.

questions.def: 'It's high time' is followed by the past simple, expressing urgency.
questions.question: It's high time you ___ a new job.

questions.def: Third conditional requires past perfect; past participle of know is 'known'.
questions.question: Had I ___, I would have acted differently.
